shared_visual_rules: Flat vector on white. OCP green #8DC63F denotes current instructional emphasis; dark gray #5F6062 supplies legible text; neutral gray #9CA3AF supplies secondary structure.
No course branding, repeated slide title, source-credit footer, edition/year badge, decorative gauges, fake measurements or arbitrary approvals inside media.
Use geometry, object movement, containment and comparison to teach; opacity is not the primary mechanism.
Exact spoken-cue emphasis takes priority over mechanically uniform scene lengths. Each major move takes approximately 0.4–1.2 seconds within its scene; keep substantial reading holds.
No audio generation, audible playback, video encoding, course edits, player edits, shared-skill edits or packaging in this proposal task.
A caption and reduced-motion final view must explain the relationship without motion. A larger media layout is not assumed; any future media_focus change needs separate review.

slides.title: A transaction crosses three agreements
slides.treatment: The same request, three different agreements
slides.learning_payoff: The learner can explain how a pair can carry an electrical signal and still fail to share the meaning of a transaction. The three layers answer different compatibility questions; they are not three independent green lights that prove interoperability.
slides.metaphor: A paired specimen under three lenses. Two persistent chiplet silhouettes sit left and right of one physical connection. The camera changes what the viewer can inspect: electrical connection, organization of transfer, then shared meaning. A single abstract read-request badge keeps its identity. A visibly separate illustrative comparison demonstrates the limitation of electrical success.
spatial_grammar: Left is sender; right is receiver. These identities never swap. Bottom is the visible physical connection; higher annotations are conceptual views, not die floorplan blocks.
Use an actual connection line only between physical endpoints. Link and protocol agreement spans are brackets between corresponding annotations, never extra wires or traffic lanes.
The request badge means one transaction concept. Its outline can acquire a transport surround, but its central read symbol remains unchanged. No fields, bits, opcodes, addresses or wire counts.

At 29.16 seconds a labelled comparison replaces the successful-meaning illustration. Preserve the earlier pair as a small still only if legible; otherwise use a clean cut headed “Illustrative mismatch”. Never silently mutate a working receiver into a broken one.
slides.creative_difference: The key motion is changing the level of inspection and preserving the same request through a representation change. The mismatch is a controlled comparison in which the electrical connection remains visible while shared meaning is missing.

scenes.spoken_cue: The physical layer, often called the P H Y, defines the electrical connection.
scenes.physical_change: Start close on the facing edges of two chiplets, already in view. From 2.84–4.10 trace the schematic connection between their physical endpoints. A single short highlight traverses it once; it is an explanatory signal cue, not a sampled waveform or startup sequence.
scenes.hold: 4.10–4.84: connection holds.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Establish the physical relationship before any higher-level interpretation.

scenes.spoken_cue: Pinout, voltages, timing, and the channel must be compatible.
scenes.physical_change: Keep the connection fixed. A short comparison bracket spans the two endpoints. Along it, change one concise label at a time as each spoken constraint arrives; the viewpoint gently widens to leave room for the transfer view. Do not align pins, draw voltage values, or time a waveform.
scenes.hold: 7.94–9.04: “Must be compatible” and the connection remain still.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Explain compatibility without fabricating a particular interface.

scenes.spoken_cue: The link layer organizes transfer across that connection.
scenes.physical_change: Widen to include a plain information ribbon beside the physical connection. A pair of open brackets closes around a portion of the ribbon, then travels across once. The bracket is an illustrative unit of organized transfer, not a frame-format diagram. Keep the physical line as the foundation.
scenes.hold: 11.40–12.26: organized unit at receiving side.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Make organization of transfer distinct from the electrical channel.

scenes.spoken_cue: Depending on the interface, it can include framing, error protection, and flow control.
scenes.physical_change: The moving unit stops. Retain a fixed “Interface-dependent” qualifier. Introduce the three terms as one compact two-line annotation beside the link bracket, then move only an underline to each named term. No shield activates, gate blocks traffic, checksum appears, or retry runs.
scenes.hold: 16.02–16.94: qualifier and examples stay still.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Make applicability explicit without visually prescribing mechanisms.

scenes.spoken_cue: The protocol gives the transferred information meaning.
scenes.physical_change: Reframe upward to reveal interpretation labels over both chiplets. Keep the link and physical connection as smaller context below. The abstract information badge acquires a central read symbol but does not move yet.
scenes.hold: 18.42–19.80: hold the two corresponding interpretation positions.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Introduce meaning as a separate question.

scenes.spoken_cue: A request to read memory must be interpreted consistently by the sender and receiver.
scenes.physical_change: At 19.88 a single “Read memory” badge leaves the sender interpretation position. It crosses on the already established transport relationship and arrives by 22.04. The receiver interpretation label becomes the same “Read memory”; align the two text baselines with an open comparison bracket. Do not show returned data or completion.
scenes.hold: 22.80–24.56: the two matching meanings hold together.
scenes.teaching_purpose: The same arriving information must have the same intended meaning.

scenes.spoken_cue: A protocol adapter can map an on-chip bus onto the die-to-die transport.
scenes.physical_change: Zoom toward the sender, keeping receiver as context. Show the same read badge at an “On-chip bus” rail. As it crosses a narrow neutral connector labelled “Adapter”, its plain outer contour becomes the abstract transport surround; its read symbol stays constant. Park it at “D2D transport”. This is a local explanatory inset of representation mapping, not a second transaction or a mandatory block placement.
scenes.hold: 28.14–29.16: unchanged meaning inside the changed surround.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Teach mapping while preserving transaction identity.

scenes.spoken_cue: A successful electrical link is therefore necessary but insufficient.
scenes.physical_change: Cut to “Illustrative mismatch”. Keep a continuous electrical connection and a single signal highlight underneath. Above, the same read badge reaches the receiver interpretation position, where an unjoined comparison bracket and “Meaning differs” identify the mismatch. Do not depict dropped bits, an actual error response, retry, or a particular incorrect memory operation.
scenes.hold: 32.06–33.06: hold both facts in the same frame.
scenes.teaching_purpose: A counterexample prevents the learner from equating physical success with transaction compatibility.

scenes.spoken_cue: The complete pair must agree on all applicable layers and options, including behavior during initialization and errors.
scenes.physical_change: Keep the mismatch specimen visible. A single enclosing bracket expands around the full pair and its three conceptual relationships; label it “All applicable layers + options”. Place “Initialization · errors” under that requirement at the start of the sentence, then emphasize each term on its spoken cue. Keep the mismatch unresolved: a requirement is not a proof of compliance.
scenes.hold: 34.60–39.522857: main comparison geometry holds; only cue emphasis changes. After 38.96 all motion stops.
scenes.teaching_purpose: End on the full compatibility obligation without inventing a recovery mechanism.

cue_events.action: Emphasize Errors; hold to audio end.

slides.caption: An electrical connection alone does not establish a valid transaction. The pair must share the applicable transfer rules, meaning, options, and behavior during initialization and errors.

poster.description: Final mismatch specimen: electrically connected chiplets, visibly differing meaning, and the bracket requiring agreement on all applicable layers and options. “Illustrative mismatch” remains visible.

slides.reduced_motion: A static mismatch comparison with three concise lines: “Physical: connection”, “Link: applicable transfer rules”, “Protocol: shared meaning”. Retain the complete-pair requirement and “Initialization · errors”. Use the caption for the longer explanation; no automatic motion.
technical_limits: The three conceptual views are illustrative; they do not prescribe where every standard assigns functions.
No BoW/UCIe packet layout, bit count, CRC, mandatory flow control, or startup/error-handling algorithm.
No electrical trace with numeric axes, rates or physical timing. Motion timing is for teaching only.
The adapter example demonstrates mapping; no performance, universal bus support, or compatibility guarantee is implied.
The mismatch is a separate comparison case, not an unexplained failure after a successful transaction. No read response is fabricated.
slides.excluded_enrichment: A concrete protocol mismatch, detailed read-response exchange, CRC/retry example, or initialization state machine would need newly approved explanatory narration and interface-specific evidence. These are excluded.

slides.title: Test what exists at each stage
slides.treatment: The connection that did not exist yet
slides.learning_payoff: The learner can point to the assembled inter-die path and explain why an earlier wafer test could not have established that completed path. They can also explain why later tests add evidence without erasing the value of early screening.
slides.metaphor: An assembly workbench with two incoming material flows and a growing test boundary. A wafer supplies identifiable dies; a separately drawn substrate arrives from a second lane. Assembly creates a new relationship between the same objects. The closing comparison uses labelled stage snapshots, not a rewind.
spatial_grammar: The upper incoming lane contains a circular silicon wafer and die silhouettes. The lower lane contains a long flat package substrate with a distinct outline. They do not morph into each other.
Die A and die B retain their notches and labels through dicing, assembly and system integration. Two dies are an illustrative simplification, not a required package count.
A thin scope bracket denotes what is being tested. It is not a test access wire, coverage map, passing result, or probe architecture.
The inter-die path is absent before assembly. A substrate-only trace may exist beforehand, but the completed path through both die interfaces appears only after assembly.
Closing snapshots carry “Before assembly”, “After assembly” and “System” labels. They are comparisons of evidence scope, not extra packages moving backwards through a factory.
slides.creative_difference: Assembly itself changes the question that can be asked. The animation makes a new connection appear only when the physical objects join, then preserves that before/after fact while contrasting stage evidence. No invented defect must disappear later.

scenes.spoken_cue: Wafer-level testing probes the individual dies before the wafer is diced.
scenes.physical_change: Start on a circular wafer with a few unlabelled die outlines and two identifiable dies A and B. A simple probe silhouette descends to one die, lifts and moves to the other before the word “diced”. The wafer remains intact throughout this sentence. Do not depict sacrificial pads or a specific test-access route.
scenes.hold: 3.74–4.54: probe lifted; intact wafer holds.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Establish the object that exists during wafer sort.

scenes.spoken_cue: It screens functionality and electrical behavior at that stage.
scenes.physical_change: A scope bracket encloses one die on the intact wafer; the wafer edge stays in view. Display “Function + electrical behavior”. Keep all die interiors neutral: no green “known good” stamp or made-up defective-die pattern.
scenes.hold: 6.84–8.02: scope stays confined to the die.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Testing supplies evidence with a stage-specific scope.

scenes.spoken_cue: Additional die-level screening can be appropriate before expensive assembly.
scenes.physical_change: At the new sentence, separate die A and B from the wafer along existing grid lines and translate them to a small pre-assembly work area. A dashed optional detour places a scope bracket around one isolated die. Label “Additional screening, as appropriate”. The wafer remains a separate residual object off to the left.
scenes.hold: 10.68–12.20: separated dies hold above an empty assembly position.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Separate dicing and optional extra screening from the preceding wafer test.

scenes.spoken_cue: Package substrate checks can occur in a parallel manufacturing flow;
scenes.physical_change: Pan slightly downward to reveal a separate substrate entering along the lower lane from outside the wafer route. Its long rectangular geometry and edge marks remain distinct. A second scope bracket inspects the substrate alone; the two dies wait above in the first lane.
scenes.hold: 14.04–15.76: show both incoming flows together.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Make parallel manufacturing physically unambiguous.

scenes.spoken_cue: a package substrate is not the same thing as the silicon wafer.
scenes.physical_change: Hold the circular wafer as a small upper-left reference and the rectangular substrate as the larger lower-right object. Keep two separate origin trails; no arrow runs from wafer to substrate. Set dies above the substrate with an obvious gap, preparing assembly without yet forming the completed connection.
scenes.hold: 17.14–19.36: side-by-side distinction and separated components hold.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Prevent the mistaken inference that the substrate is sliced from the wafer.

scenes.spoken_cue: After assembly, new connections and new failure opportunities exist.
scenes.physical_change: Capture a labelled still of the separated components at left. In the main view, lower the same dies onto the same substrate; by 20.34 the placement is complete. On “new connections”, draw one highlighted continuous path from A through the package to B. Keep the earlier snapshot without a completed path. Use a simple conceptual top view; no bump count, bond technology or package cross-section.
scenes.hold: 21.24–23.28: hold before/after comparison; the new path remains neutral, not passed.
scenes.teaching_purpose: The assembled connection is a new test object; no earlier test could have inspected the completed path itself.

cue_events.action: Complete path becomes visible only now.
Emphasize New path; introduce no specific defect.

scenes.spoken_cue: Package testing must address those inter-die paths and the accessible functions.
scenes.physical_change: The scope bracket widens around the assembled package. A focal highlight follows the entire conceptual A-to-B relationship once, then rests over a generic die interior to indicate accessible functions. Do not route a test signal through a supposed JTAG/BIST port or claim that everything is accessible.
scenes.hold: 26.38–28.00: hold package scope with both objects identifiable.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Package testing adds the assembled path and accessible-function questions.

scenes.spoken_cue: System-level testing then checks integrated behavior under relevant operating conditions.
scenes.physical_change: Move the complete package, without altering its internal identities, into an outlined system board. Expand the scope bracket around that integrated context. An incoming stimulus token and an outgoing behavior token appear on opposite sides of the system boundary; move once through the context without a pass/fail result. Use “Relevant conditions” as text, not numeric knobs or a thermal color map.
scenes.hold: 30.98–32.82: system context holds.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Integrated behavior is an additional scope of evidence.

scenes.spoken_cue: These stages complement each other.
scenes.physical_change: Reframe to three large labelled snapshots: isolated die evidence, assembled connection, system context. Use the same A/B notches in each. The substrate enters the assembly snapshot along its separate lower branch. Join the three scope brackets with one baseline labelled “Complementary evidence”, not with a moving factory arrow.
scenes.hold: 33.98–34.78: comparison composition is fully settled.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Integrate the three questions without implying that later tests replace earlier ones.

scenes.spoken_cue: Passing wafer sort does not prove the final package,
scenes.physical_change: In the settled comparison, emphasize the early die scope and the assembled path together. A dashed comparison connector stops at the edge of the new path, labelled “New after assembly”. No certificate is transferred; no already-tested package turns red.
scenes.hold: 36.30–37.66: simultaneous early-scope/new-path hold.
scenes.teaching_purpose: The missing connection before assembly explains why early evidence is insufficient for the package.

scenes.spoken_cue: and a final system test does not replace economical early defect screening.
scenes.physical_change: Retain the identical comparison layout. Shift emphasis from the new path to the early screening scope while the system stays visible. The baseline remains “Complementary evidence”. No reverse-flow arrow or removal of early testing.
scenes.hold: 39.84–41.659637: all motion stops; the three scopes remain available for comparison.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Later integrated testing does not recover the economical benefit of screening before expensive assembly.

slides.caption: Wafer and die screening, package tests, and system tests examine different physical states. The assembled inter-die path needs later testing, while early screening still avoids spending assembly effort on identified defects.

poster.description: Three labelled physical-state snapshots with persistent die identities: die before assembly, new assembled path, and system context. Keep the separate substrate input visible and the baseline “Complementary evidence”.

slides.reduced_motion: Use the final three snapshots. Label the die “Early screening”, the assembled path “New after assembly”, and the system “Integrated behavior”. Show the substrate on a separate incoming branch; use the caption to explain why each scope matters.
technical_limits: The wafer and substrate are distinct objects and independent flows. No wafer-to-substrate morph or connecting arrow.
No completed inter-die path exists in the pre-assembly snapshot. The substrate may contain conductors before assembly, but the full die-to-die relationship does not.
No universal test access path, test-vector content, coverage percentage, yield statistic, or defect frequency.
No green die stamps or known-good guarantees. “Screening” states purpose, not an assertion that all faults were found.
The recommended sequence deliberately shows a new test obligation rather than a fault that would require an unnarrated repair or alternate-unit transition.
A two-die package and plain board are illustrative objects, not an implied required construction or test order for every technology.
slides.excluded_enrichment: A specific open/short fault, repair, yield loss or defect escape story would need additional narration or an explicit comparison reset. A detailed probe/test access sequence would require technology-specific evidence. Neither is recommended for this locked clip.

slides.title: From a catalog to an evaluable system
slides.treatment: Move the question; keep the model
slides.learning_payoff: The learner can distinguish the information exchanged for shared analysis from the detailed implementation that remains supplier-controlled, and recognize that this boundary still needs policies and evidence for both accuracy and confidentiality.
slides.metaphor: A question travels to an immovable model across a visibly labelled organizational boundary; only a permitted answer returns. The boundary is ownership, not a magical security wall. A later inspection exposes the policy questions attached to the model, incoming request and outgoing result.
spatial_grammar: Integrator occupies the left side; Supplier occupies the right side. One supplier is a legibility-focused exemplar, not a mandated federation topology.
The detailed model is a solid neutral slab with a distinct corner notch; it stays at the same supplier-relative position for the entire sequence, including camera reframing.

Request and boundary conditions travel left-to-right; permitted results travel right-to-left on a separate clearly labelled return path. Their shapes differ from the model and never detach pieces from it.
The vertical supplier boundary persists. No padlock, shield, encrypted tunnel or gate animation asserts security. A small “Initial proof of concept” status label is visible from the opening.
Policy annotations use question wording and neutral outlines. No checkmark, authorization success state or guaranteed confidentiality result appears.
slides.creative_difference: The governing visual invariant is that the model never crosses. Instead of a generic three-step workflow, the learner sees different information take different routes and then inspects where policy obligations attach to that exchange.

scenes.spoken_cue: Federated simulation explores a useful idea:
scenes.physical_change: Begin with the integrator and supplier regions already visible, separated by a clear vertical ownership boundary. Place the detailed model in the supplier region. Keep a small neutral “Initial proof of concept” label at the upper edge of the diagram, not as course branding.
scenes.hold: 1.82–3.24: spatial relationship holds.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Frame the entire sequence as a proposed direction, not an operating service.

scenes.spoken_cue: bring an agreed simulation request to the supplier's model rather than requiring the supplier to hand over the model.
scenes.physical_change: A distinct question-shaped token labelled “Agreed request” crosses toward the supplier and docks beside the model by 5.86. At “hand over the model”, hold the model firmly in place and emphasize its supplier-side anchoring line. Do not animate a model attempting to leave or being blocked.
scenes.hold: 6.36–9.38: request beside model; model stays still.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Make the direction of movement memorable while preserving ownership.

cue_events.action: Emphasize the stationary model, with no export animation.

scenes.spoken_cue: An integrator could exchange boundary conditions and receive permitted results while the detailed implementation remains under supplier control.
scenes.physical_change: A thin conditions strip follows the request inward at 10.20–11.74. At 11.86 a separate result token originates beside the model and returns to the integrator, arriving by 13.38. Its contour and fill differ from the model, with no numeric plot or values. On the final clause, keep both endpoints visible and emphasize the model anchored inside the supplier region.
scenes.hold: 14.90–17.08: result at integrator, detailed model at supplier, both visible.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Distinguish exchangeable boundary information from detailed implementation.

cue_events.action: Model stays fixed; supplier boundary emphasized.

scenes.spoken_cue: That arrangement needs more than a secure container.
scenes.physical_change: Hold the exchange and reframe closer to the model and both paths. Bring three neutral policy annotations into reading positions: one attached to model identity, one beside incoming requests, one beside outgoing results. These are questions, not executed controls. A faint container outline may remain around the model, but it never turns green or gets a padlock.
scenes.hold: 19.26–19.76: all three questions settled before the rapid noun list.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Expose the missing obligations without pretending a container solves them.

scenes.spoken_cue: Model identity, version, authorization, query limits, and permitted outputs all affect confidentiality and trust in the result.
scenes.physical_change: Keep all three short policy questions in fixed positions. Move a thin emphasis underline between their terms on the exact spoken cues. Tie identity/version to the model, authorization/query limits to incoming requests, and permitted outputs to the returning results. No request is denied or approved, and no query count or result filtering algorithm is invented.
scenes.hold: 24.28–27.42: all three groups remain legible together; no new motion.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Policy questions apply to different parts of the exchange and remain obligations.

cue_events.action: Underline version in the same label.

scenes.spoken_cue: The Summit proposal describes an initial proof-of-concept direction rather than an approved universal service.
scenes.physical_change: Pull back gently to the original ownership view. Keep the question annotations as three small attachment marks rather than miniature text if necessary. Briefly emphasize the existing “Initial proof of concept” status, then return it to its quiet state. Do not show a service portal, marketplace approval, certification, or completed deployment.
scenes.hold: 30.20–33.24: full exchange relationship holds.
scenes.teaching_purpose: The diagram teaches a proposal without laundering it into an established service.

scenes.spoken_cue: Its teaching value is the relationship between shared analysis and protected implementation.
scenes.physical_change: Draw two open brackets: one encloses the exchanged request/conditions/result relationship and is labelled “Shared analysis”; the other encloses the stationary detailed model and is labelled “Supplier-controlled model”. Keep a single supplier boundary between them. The brackets describe different scopes and never close into a seal.
scenes.hold: 35.50–38.34: the two scopes hold in one view.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Separate participation in analysis from disclosure of implementation.

scenes.spoken_cue: Accuracy and confidentiality both require explicit policies and evidence.
scenes.physical_change: Keep the established exchange diagram. Add two equally weighted short requirement lines below it: “Accuracy: policies + evidence” and “Confidentiality: policies + evidence”. Use neutral text and an open evidence bracket, not gauges or checks. Settle both by 40.06; underline “policies + evidence” as the final words arrive.
scenes.hold: 40.06–42.679546: all geometry holds; final underline is complete by 42.12.
scenes.teaching_purpose: Neither model custody nor a returned result proves the two desired properties.

cue_events.action: Underline policies + evidence in both lines.

slides.caption: The initial proof-of-concept direction brings agreed requests and boundary conditions to supplier-controlled models and returns permitted results. Accuracy and confidentiality still depend on explicit policies and evidence.

poster.description: Integrator and supplier separated by the ownership boundary; requests/conditions in and permitted results out; detailed model remains at supplier. Retain initial proof-of-concept status and the two evidence requirements.

slides.reduced_motion: Use the final ownership diagram with two labelled arrow directions and the model wholly inside the supplier region. Keep the PoC status and the two concise evidence lines. Put the five policy topics in the caption or adjacent accessible description if they are too small in the poster; never shrink all of them into the image.
technical_limits: This is the Summit proposal’s initial proof-of-concept direction, not a deployed or universally approved simulation service.
The supplier boundary represents control of the model, not a proven secure execution or network mechanism.
No normative orchestrator, network protocol, crypto scheme, simulator API, cloud topology or universal federation architecture.
No model bytes, source, or apparent model fragments cross the boundary. Only conceptual requests, boundary conditions and permitted results move.
No quantitative outputs or fabricated accuracy/confidentiality evidence. Any result is a labelled abstract token, not a claim of successful analysis.
The deck’s initial PoC scope is power plus thermal; this recommendation uses domain-neutral results. It does not imply initial support for SI, PI, mechanics or functional simulation.
Identity/version/authorization/query/output annotations remain requirements and questions; they never become arbitrary approvals.
slides.excluded_enrichment: A simulator workflow, worked power/thermal example, adversarial model-extraction demonstration, or policy enforcement/denial sequence would require extra approved narration and specific evidence. The locked clip does not explain these actions, so they are excluded.

review_checklist: Approve the specific teaching relationship and visual metaphor for each slide; all three preserve locked narration.
Approve the opt-in synchronized single-pass mode for these selected figures before production; this document records a proposal, not approval.
